evidence.text: Archer has made no cash equity raise in 2026; its last three were registered directs in Feb 2025 ($302m), Jun 2025 ($850m) and Nov 2025 ($650m, announced with the Q3 2025 print, which fell -7.88%). Cash plus short-term investments was $1.56bn at 30 June, down $215m in Q2. H1 2026 operating cash use was $305.5m against $198m a year earlier. In H1 the company settled $70.6m of vendor obligations with 11.1m shares, and on 2026-08-18 issued another 8.26m shares to vendors for services and goods. The pending Boeing deal is paid in stock. This keeps open a meaningful chance of another raise with or right after this print, at a share price near multi-year lows.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 (2025-11-06): EPS beat with a $650m raise announced alongside; stock -7.88% (baseline; TipRanks headline 'beats Q3 EPS but stock falls as investors focus on dilution and high costs').
evidence.why_not_priced: No offering has been filed (no 424B5 since August; the only 424B7 is the vendor resale), so the market can only guess at a raise. Most of the inference is priced by the skew (+6.2 downside paid). If a raise were fully expected, the stock would not have run up 21% into the print with calls dominating open interest. On what the money buys: certification Phase 4, eIPP operations and Boeing integration. None of these is corroborated by revenue or backlog, so this is not a ramp-funding raise. It stays a negative, sized small because it is an inference.
evidence.independence: Q2 10-Q vendor-share settlement $70.6m (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001824502/000182450226000059/achr-20260630.htm) and the Q2 release cash walk (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001824502/000182450226000056/archerq226earningspressr.htm). evidence.text: The HSR waiting period on Archer's all-stock purchase of Boeing's Wisk, Insitu and SkyGrid expired 2026-09-18, and the company expects to close by end-2026, with 'additional regulatory approvals' still underway. evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 print (2026-08-10), where the deal was announced: +8.47%, the second-best reaction in the last eight.
evidence.why_not_priced: Pro-forma numbers have not been published, and the stock is down about 45% since the deal was announced. That fall suggests the market gives the deal little value and treats the share issuance as a cost. If a pro-forma outlook were priced in, the stock would not sit at its 52-week low. A slip in timing, a regulatory snag (Insitu is a defence contractor) or a large issuance count would be negative, which is why the range is wide.
evidence.independence: Q2 release (Insitu adds >$200m revenue) https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001824502/000182450226000056/archerq226earningspressr.htm. evidence.text: Thirteen BlueBirds were in orbit at the 2026-08-10 update, the last launch was BB11-13 on 2026-08-05, and BB14-16 were 'ready to ship' with no launch date announced in the three months since. The company announces launches about two months ahead. Its 2026-11-06 8-K describes external launch agreements for >100 BlueBirds 'spread over 2027 and 2028'. Reaching 'approximately 45 in orbit by early 2027' would mean about 32 satellites in a few months, so the print most likely re-times that target. Market expectation: Piper Sandler cut its YE2026 forecast from 45 to 18 on 2026-10-13. The company has not yet conceded the 45 target.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-07-15: the last re-timing of the 45-satellite target (end-2026 to early 2027), announced with a $1B convert, was followed by -17.04% (baseline). 2026-04 BB7 wrong orbit: the stock slid (rallies.ai, 2026-04-23).

The company itself still carries '~45 by early 2027' (Trefis 2026-11-03 repeats it as the live target). An explicit reset to a later date or a lower count, with no BB14-16 date, would be a new company statement. If the market had fully priced a reset, the Oct 13 downgrade would have been the bottom. Instead the stock fell another 30% after it, on competition and dilution news rather than on the schedule.

evidence.text: The Q3 report gives the first cash walk since the July $1.15B convert. Inputs: cash $2.29B plus $428M restricted (Ligado bridge) at June 30, plus the $1.15B convert (about $3.3B usable pro forma); Q3 capex guided $350-425M; H1 FCF -$1.0B. On top of this sits the 2026-11-06 Firefly deal ($400M cash plus 10-14M shares upfront, then $500M over three years). Analysts put cash burn at about $3.1B from July 2026 through 2028 before Firefly. Any ATM use in Q3 under the October 2025 equity distribution agreement, or a new raise plan, lands at this print.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Financing days were sold hard: 2026-07-15 convert -17.04%, 2026-02-11 registered direct plus convert -15.17%, 2025-10-21 -9.24% (baseline, non-earnings). But the 2026-11-06 Firefly commitment of $1.3B, partly in stock, was bought +1% (Reuters via bdnews24) to +7% (TIKR).
evidence.why_not_priced: The Sept 30 balance and any Q3 ATM issuance are not public until the 10-Q and release. The market bought the Firefly news, which suggests it has not netted the $400M cash and 3-5% dilution against the runway. The answer on what the money buys matters here: it funds launch capacity, the binding constraint, and $1.3B of backlog corroborates demand. It does not help 2027 deployments, and no going-concern flag appears. So the finding is a small negative, not a distress call.
evidence.independence: Same document as finding 1 for the Firefly terms (8-K ex99-1, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1780312/000149315226050513/ex99-1.htm). EBITDA $875-975M, Paramount+ subs 'flattish' q/q, ~$200M transformation costs (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2041610/000204161026000052/ex99_q226.htm). So the bar is the company guide. There is no sourced bar for the combined company's 2027 or synergy outlook, which is the line the stock most likely trades on, so the guidance findings are capped at moderate size.
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest 145.86M shares (settlement 2026-10-15), 3.56% of a 4.10B float, days to cover ~3.5-4.0 (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/skyd/statistics/ ; https://stockmarketwatch.com/stock/SKYD/short-interest). Not a crowded short. Baseline skew is -25.5 vol points (25d call IV well above put IV: upside paid) with put/call OI 0.16. The option market leans long, so a long lean here agrees with the skew and is partly priced. Spot $8.285 is -50.5% from the 52w high and +21.8% from the 52w low. 20d run-up -9.55% is distorted by the 2026-10-14 warrant ex-date, a -22% close to $7.06 against a $0.19 NYSE mechanical adjustment (https://www.thewrap.com/industry-news/business/skydance-warrants-issued-stock-reaction/). 5d run-up +2.66%. The stock trades below the $12 equity-financing price and below the $12 warrant strike, a supply overhang. Consensus rating Hold or Reduce, average target ~$9.15.

evidence.text: First print after close, and the company tends to raise its savings targets: at the first post-Skydance-merger print (10 Nov 2025) it raised the cost-savings target from $2B to $3B, gave its first FY guide, and the stock rose +9.8% (15.25 to 16.74) despite missing estimates; at Q2 2026 it raised run-rate efficiencies from $2.5B to $2.7B. The current public target is >=$6B run-rate synergies within three years, 3.0x net leverage by end-2029 and >$10B FCF in 2030 (6 Oct 2026 closing release). Debtwire's base case credits only $1.75B by 2027 and puts net leverage at 6.16x on realised synergies, so the market discounts the target heavily (stock below the $12 financing price). An early quantification or upsizing on this call lands against a sceptical bar.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: On the same CIK, the Nov 2025 first post-merger print raised the savings target and set the first FY guide: +9.8% next session. The Feb 2026 print (FY guide reiterated, $30B revenue): +10.0%. Closes from Yahoo chart v8 (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/SKYD?range=1y&interval=1d).
evidence.why_not_priced: If the market believed the $6B target, the equity would trade nearer the $12 at which the financing investors bought, and Debtwire would not model 29% of it by 2027. The stock is -50% from its high, and the 2026-10-14 credit report models a fraction of the target. No new synergy number has been published since close, so any quantification on the call is new information.
evidence.independence: Savings-target precedent: https://senalnews.com/en/data/paramount-skydance-reports-q3-loss-after-merger-but-sets-new-strategy-for-growth (2025-11-11). Q2 efficiency raise: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2041610/000204161026000052/ex99_q226.htm. Debtwire scepticism: https://ionanalytics.com/insights/debtwire/skydance-corporation-synergies-alone-wont-hit-leverage-targets-credit-report/ (2026-10-14). The sign of this finding is inference from precedent, not a document.

evidence.text: Legacy Paramount beat its own Q2 adj. EBITDA guide by a wide margin ($1,099M actual against a $0.9-1.0B guide, +16% vs midpoint) and raised FY26 to $3.8-3.9B. The Q3 guide of $875-975M was framed as lower on content-amortisation timing, so it is a conservative bar the company has a record of clearing; expect Q3 EBITDA at or above the top of the range.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 EBITDA beat and FY raise (4 Aug 2026): +4.5% next session (8.38 to 8.76). Q1 2026 (4 May): -4.2% (11.13 to 10.66) with a same-day analyst downgrade. Both from Yahoo chart v8 closes.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the beat habit is visible. It is sized small because the reported quarter belongs to a pre-close standalone entity that the stock no longer trades on. Aggregator EPS bars ($0.11-0.13) and revenue bars ($7.6B, $16.48B) disagree, so nobody holds a clean bar on this line.
evidence.independence: The Fox proxy finding below points the same way through the ad line. It is a different source (Fox 8-K / TheDesk).

evidence.text: The ad market in the Sep quarter ran hot for broadcast. Fox's fiscal Q1 2027 (quarter to 30 Sep 2026) had TV advertising +60.1% and total ad revenue +47% to $2.08B, and political ads above $350M, a midterm record, with over $250M on owned stations. CBS's network and owned stations share the midterm political cycle and NFL season. Fox's World Cup (Jun-Jul) has no CBS equivalent, so the transmission is partial.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No separate history on the ad line for this name. TV Media ad surprises have been overshadowed by deal news on every print since the Nov 2025 merger.
evidence.why_not_priced: Fox's print landed after Skydance last spoke about the quarter (its guide was set 4 Aug). Paramount's guide presumably assumed some political revenue, but a record cycle on a peer's stations suggests upside to the TV Media ad line that the stale Aug guide does not reflect. If it were priced, the Q3 consensus would sit above the guide range, and the aggregator numbers do not show that clearly.
evidence.independence: Proxy only. Neither the company nor a direct counterparty has confirmed CBS political dollars. Fox SEC 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001754301/000162828026068663/foxearningsreleaseq127.htm

evidence.text: Leverage is the bear line. S&P cut the rating to BB on projected ~7.6x leverage lasting into 2027. The company issued second-lien notes at 8.25-9.125% coupons ($6.0B 2031, $4.0B 2034, $1.4B 2036). Debtwire models 6.16x net leverage on realised synergies, with covenant headroom relying on credited synergies. The pro forma balance sheet carries $82.4B of debt. A combined-company FCF or transformation-cost frame weaker than the 3.0x-by-2029 path would hit the equity.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: On the day leverage concerns and the S&P cut hit (bond deal, late Sep/early Oct 2026), the stock fell as much as 9% intraday and closed down about 5% (https://parameter.io/investors-punish-paramount-skydance-psky-over-leverage-concerns-as-wbd-deal-nears-close/).
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the stock is -50% from its high and the leverage is public. It stays filed because the first combined cash-flow, interest and transformation-cost numbers arrive on this call. The financing question has a clear answer: the money bought WBD, not a ramp, so the sign is negative but small. The size is cut because the skew (-25.5, calls paid) argues against a downside print.
evidence.independence: Second-lien terms are in the same 8-K family as the pro forma (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002041610/000110465926113913/tm2626659d7_ex99-2.htm). The S&P BB cut is via parameter.io. This finding and the synergy finding are two sides of the combined outlook; they share the 6 Oct targets as their reference but rest on different facts (synergy precedent vs leverage arithmetic).
